payload.headline: Strong bounce day, but SPY and QQQ remain below their 50-day averages

summary.thesis: The long-term uptrend still holds for both indices, but the short-term trend is broken. Only 25% of stocks sit above their own 50-day average, while fear is in the 'normal' range.
summary.decision: Be selective. The long-term picture is intact, but most stocks are not taking part, and QQQ still fails the pipeline's 'above its 50-day average' market check.
summary.act_at: QQQ close above 718.87 (50-day average) to lean in more; QQQ close below 680.65 or SPY close below 728.65 (200-day averages) to stand aside.

payload.happening: On 2026-11-11, SPY closed at 759.81, up 1.32% from 749.92. QQQ closed at 690.38, up 2.31% from 674.76. The rally came after a pullback: both indices set 1-month closing lows on Nov 5 (SPY 733.0, QQQ 647.05). Over 20 trading days SPY is still down 1.27% and QQQ is down 5.29%. Over 5 days they are down 0.91% and 0.23%. Both remain under the past year's highest closes of 779.09 (SPY) and 759.66 (QQQ), both set on Oct 6. The VIX fear gauge fell from about 19.46 to about 17.49. No news has been reported since the last note. Coming up: PPI producer-price data on Nov 13 at 08:30, and NVDA earnings, with an estimated date of Nov 17 after the close.
payload.business: Trend: both indices are labeled 'sideways'. Each is above its 200-day average (SPY 728.65, QQQ 680.65), so the long trend holds. Each is below its 50-day average (SPY 764.55, QQQ 718.87), so the short trend is broken. SPY is only 0.6% below its 50-day line, while QQQ is 4.1% below its own, so tech is the weaker part. Fear: the VIX is in the 'normal' 15–20 band, at the 56th percentile of its past 252 days. Investors are not panicking, and they are not complacent either. Breadth: 25% of stocks are above their 50-day average. Together, these readings point to a market that is calm on the surface but narrow underneath. The index bounce is not yet matched by most individual stocks. (General knowledge: narrow participation often makes index gains less durable until more stocks join in.) The pipeline's market gate is not active.

worth.text: DATA has no valuation inputs (earnings, multiples or yields) for SPY or QQQ, so this note makes no fair-value estimate. The only reference points are the price levels in the trend gates.
worth.key_assumption: No valuation is implied. The levels cited are trend references, not estimates of worth.

bull: Both SPY and QQQ remain above their 200-day averages (728.65 and 680.65), so the long-term trend counts as up.
The Nov 5 one-month lows (SPY 733.0, QQQ 647.05) are holding, and Nov 11 brought a strong bounce: SPY +1.32%, QQQ +2.31%.
Fear is 'normal': the VIX fell to about 17.49 from about 19.46, at the 56th percentile of its past year.
bear: Both indices sit below their 50-day averages, so the short-term trend is broken. QQQ is 4.1% below its 50-day line at 718.87.
Breadth is weak: only 25% of stocks are above their 50-day average, so the rally is narrow.
QQQ is down 5.29% over 20 days and sits 5.6% below its 1-month high of 728.95. NVDA earnings (estimated Nov 17) could move the whole tech group either way.

levels.what: SPY 50-day average: a close above it would put SPY's short-term trend back up.
SPY 1-month high (Oct 21): a close above it would mean SPY's pullback is fully recovered.
QQQ 50-day average: a close above it would put the short-term trend back up and pass the pipeline's market check. That would be the cue to lean in more.
QQQ 1-month high (Oct 14): a close above it would mean the tech pullback is fully recovered.
SPY 1-month low (Nov 5): a close below it would mean the decline is continuing.
SPY 200-day average: a close below it would put the long-term trend down. That would be a stand-aside signal.
QQQ 200-day average: a close below it would put tech's long-term trend down. That would be a stand-aside signal.
QQQ 1-month low (Nov 5): a close below it would mean the tech decline is continuing.

longterm.why: The long-term trend holds and fear is normal, which argues against standing aside. The broken short-term trend and 25% breadth argue against leaning in broadly. That combination favors only the strongest names over broad buying.

swing.why: QQQ is below its 50-day average of 718.87. Per the trend gates, setups keep failing the pipeline's market check until QQQ closes above that level.

decision.timing: PPI comes on Nov 13 at 08:30, and NVDA reports earnings on an estimated Nov 17, after the close. Both are near-term events that could move the indices toward or away from the gate levels.

change_mind: More constructive: QQQ closes above 718.87 and SPY closes above 764.55, putting both short-term trends back up. Ideally breadth would also rise from 25%.
More defensive: SPY closes below 728.65 or QQQ closes below 680.65, putting the long-term trend down. A close below the 1-month lows (SPY 733.0, QQQ 647.05) would also signal a continuing decline.
payload.what_changed: This is the first note, so there is no earlier note to compare against. Since the previous close, SPY rose 1.32% and QQQ rose 2.31%, and the VIX fell from about 19.46 to about 17.49. No news has been reported since the last note.
